about: When a crop grows in an origin — the season a calibration's weather is read over (E163). Annual crops and the perennials MIRCA-OS covers take their season from MIRCA-OS 2015 by one rule; olive, citrus and wine grapes from FAO-56 Table 11 rows applied to the origins listed. A crop × origin with no season here is held, never given a guessed one.

mirca_os.source: Kebede, E.A. et al. (2025), A global open-source dataset of monthly irrigated and rainfed cropped areas (MIRCA-OS) for the 21st century, Scientific Data; HydroShare doi:10.4211/hs.60a890eb841c460192c03bb590687145 — the 2015 crop calendars v0.1 (rainfed and irrigated): planting and maturity month and growing area per crop, sub-crop and spatial unit
mirca_os.country: unit_code // 10000 is the unit's UN M49 country code
mirca_os.rule: a month is in the season when at least half of the crop's growing area in the origin (all units, sub-crops, rainfed and irrigated) is between its planting and maturity month (both included); a season crossing the new year belongs to the year it matures in — its months after the maturity month are months of the previous year; the months picked must be one unbroken run (in harvest-year order), else the origin is held — several calendars in one origin are not merged into one season
mirca_os.coverage_rule: the calendars must describe at least half of the crop's harvested area in the origin as the crop map holds it (MapSPAM / CROPGRIDS 2020), else the origin is held: a calendar covering a minority of the crop (MIRCA-OS 2015 v0.1 lists 0.28 million ha of Canadian wheat, all on the winter calendar, against 9.6 million ha mapped) does not state its season (E168)

fao56.source: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D., Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Table 11: Lengths of crop development stages for various planting periods and climatic regions (days)
fao56.rule: the season is the calendar months overlapping the stated start month's first day plus the row's total days (the sum of its four stages); the row's region is applied only to the origins listed with it
fao56.mediterranean_coast_rule: FAO-56's 'Mediterranean' and the wine row's 'Mid Latitudes' are applied to the countries with a Mediterranean Sea coast (all lie between 30°N and 46°N) — no other country is given a FAO-56 season

gaps.Almonds: FAO-56 Table 11 has no almond row ('Deciduous Orchard' names no crop) — almonds are held
